title: Retail Installment Contracts Training Q&A: How Many Charges a Hardship Extension Carries
content:
*On a Retail Installment Contracts hardship extension, how many charges does the agreement carry?*

It depends on the installments the agreement defers and on the installment due on the next due date at the effective date:

- When the agreement defers **more than one** installment **and** the installment due on the next due date is past due on the effective date **and** carries partial installment credit, the number of charges is the installments deferred less the partial installment credit divided by the scheduled installment — that is, the partial credit divided by the scheduled installment is taken from the installments deferred.
- When it defers more than one installment in any other case, the number of charges is the installments deferred.
- In every other case it is **one**.

*When is the installment "past due on the effective date"?* When the next due date is earlier than the effective date.

| Installments deferred | Next due date earlier than the effective date | Partial installment credit | Number of charges |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (or none named) | any | any | 1 |
| more than 1 | yes | more than 0.00 | installments deferred less (partial credit divided by the scheduled installment) |
| more than 1 | yes | none | installments deferred |
| more than 1 | no | any | installments deferred |

*A worked figure (hypothetical contract)?* An agreement defers 2 installments; the next due date is 12 days before the effective date; partial credit of 97.25 against a scheduled installment of 389.00. 97.25 divided by 389.00 is 0.25, so the number of charges is 2 less 0.25, that is 1.75. The count is not rounded to a whole number.

*And with the same contract current on the effective date?* The number of charges is 2.
